title: Separate Schur bandwidth from the narrow inverse bound
body:
## Summary
- One scalar elimination in a bandwidth-2 witness produces a Schur complement of bandwidth 3. The filled entry is `-1/64`, and row scaling still leaves bandwidth 3 with off-diagonal infinity norm `3/7`.
- The inverse of that complement is the complementary block of the original inverse. Both of its induced norms equal `648/389`, inside the original Neumann bounds `2` and `10`.
- The inverse bound survives. The bandwidth-`b` hypothesis does not. The selected κ is unchanged.
